editions.text:
The station logged 313 feeder visits and 21 species, placing the day above the seven-day average for both metrics. Regulars such as the Northern Cardinal, Tufted Titmouse, and Carolina Chickadee held their usual positions, while the Eastern Kingbird returned after an eight-day absence. Common Grackle, Northern Flicker, and Red-breasted Nuthatch were recorded for the first time at the station, with the grackle also marking its first confident visual sighting.

Audio and visual data captured a consistent mix of daily residents, including Blue Jays and Carolina Wrens, which have been present every day this week. A single Eastern Phoebe was noted perching on a branch, adding to the six-day streak for that species. Downy Woodpecker, Pileated Woodpecker, and Song Sparrow were not recorded, consistent with their sporadic history over the past week.

The day’s activity level sat between the quiet Tuesday and the busier Wednesday of the previous period, reflecting a steady state in station usage. With no changes to feeders or audio sources, the presence of new species is treated as a station record rather than a shift in local bird populations. The numbers align with the consistent baseline established earlier in the week.
